pre_mortem: It is Monday and Smith's over lost: CHI's 39% blitz rate disrupted PHI, whose supplied EPA/dropback declines from 0.20 without blitzes to 0.12 against them; Wicks absorbed the productive throws, or PHI ran out an early lead. Smith's two-game total conceals how uneven his production may have been. Loveland's under lost because three yards on five targets was an unsustainably poor conversion of 43 air yards, not a stable ceiling. One successful downfield catch or a trailing CHI script could erase the apparent cushion. Without routes, alignment and injury information, neither counter-case is resolved strongly enough to upgrade these leans.
slip_story: Both leans fit a competitive game in which PHI earns receiving production through Smith while CHI relies on its backs and established WR opportunities rather than expanding Loveland's role. Smith also benefits from the CHI-leads flip; Loveland's under can survive a competitive or CHI-leading script. A PHI runaway threatens both through opposite volume shifts. Correlation is unmeasured, so retain as separate watchlist leans rather than manufacture a 3–4-leg slip. No TDs, duplicate-player markets or additional legs.
